title: Ballot and grade books copy every voter per vote: fold them in linear time
premise_notes: scene.ts:122 spreads poll.ballots per vote, and :232-233 respreads gradeVotes per grade. chatMemory.ts:1-5 documents the same quadratic fix for chat only. sceneModel.ts:100,211 are unbounded Records. playback.ts:35-39 refolds from 0 on a backward seek. live.ts:115 reduces per event, and App.tsx:285 calls advanceTo on render. tallies.ts:65 filters every ballot per option. Independent re-bench at HEAD (scratch vitest, distinct voters): 1000/2000/4000 votes = 59/454/2511 ms. That is superlinear as claimed, though absolute figures are about 5x lower than the card's on this run.
floor_notes: M, effort 5, impact 7, risk 4, 9 files, 6 cases, gate architecture. It must sequence after slot A (shared scene.ts/tallies.ts), and the card says so. Wall-clock cases in CI carry flake risk, but the 2 s bound and the ratio guard leave wide margins.
ambition_why: Generalises an existing persistent-map fix into a shared ViewerBook and moves tallies to O(1) aggregates. It is a real scale fix for live bursts and scrubbing.

falsifiability_why: Cases 1-3 are red at HEAD (8000 votes take far over 2 s, and the ratio is well above 8). Cases 4-6 are regression guards that pass today, but they correctly catch a mutable-map shortcut that would break retained keyframes.
reason: Measured, reproducible superlinear fold with clear linear-time and persistence guards. Build it after slot A.
